Lisa — please see consolidated responses below (suitable for inclusion in your questionnaire). I've labeled items you can copy into FinHealth_Security_Qs.xlsx: 

1) Training usage assurance (short answer):
Redwood does not use customer content from hosted or dedicated accounts to train public models by default. Any use of customer content for model training would require an explicit contractual opt-in and an internal review (privacy/legal/security).

2) What counts as "customer content" vs operational telemetry (nuances):
- Customer content: request payloads (messages/prompts), attachments, and generated outputs tied to your tenant.
- Operational telemetry: aggregated metrics and anonymized usage stats (token counts, latency distributions) used to improve platform performance. These telemetry signals are not linked back to individual customer content for model training.
- Transient operational copies: short-lived debug snapshots, request logs, and KV cache entries are created to serve requests and troubleshoot incidents, but they are treated as customer data and are excluded from training unless you opt in.

3) Retention mapping (typical defaults for hosted Redwood accounts):
- Live request cache / KV cache: ephemeral, typically evicted within minutes to hours depending on workload (default behavior).
- Request logs (operational): retained 7 days by default; available for troubleshooting and tracing.
- Debug snapshots (on-demand or incident captures): retained up to 30 days unless explicitly saved as an incident artifact.
- Backups / nightly snapshots: retained 90 days; backups are encrypted and access-controlled.
- Audit logs / admin traces: retained 1 year for compliance and billing reconciliation (access restricted).

Note: These are defaults; customer-specific retention tiers can be negotiated (e.g., 30-day or 0-day retention) on Dedicated/Private plans.

4) Deletion and purge workflows:
- Self-serve deletion API: Available for content and embeddings: https://console.redwoodinference.com/docs/api/delete-requests (you can call this to request immediate deletion of customer content).
- Purge SLA (hosted): API deletion requests are processed within 24 hours; full downstream snapshot/backups purge may take up to 7 business days depending on retention tier and backup windows. We provide a signed deletion certificate in PDF form upon completion.
- Manual purge / edge cases: For retained backups or legal-hold concerns, open a support ticket referencing your tenant ID and we’ll provide a remediation timeline.

5) Hosted vs Private (VPC/on-prem) differences: 
- Hosted (Redwood-managed): We maintain the retention defaults above; Redwood personnel may access operational copies under strict RBAC for support/incident response. Access is logged and audited.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): Similar retention controls but can be tuned per contract; access controls are stricter and can be limited to fewer operational engineers.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): Customer data remains in your network; Redwood has no access to tenant content unless you enable support access. No hosted backups occur unless arranged. This is the recommended model if FinHealth requires complete separation.

6) Evidence and attestations:
- We will provide: (a) a one-page signed deletion confirmation upon purge completion, (b) SOC 2 Type II summary and scope, and (c) redacted audit logs showing the purge ticket.

Attachments provided: redwood-retention-matrix-v1.pdf (retention defaults)

If you need tighter windows for certain data classes (e.g., 0-day logs, encrypted ephemeral only), we can scope that in the contract.

Best,
Neha
